title: Postgres backup restore
body: Restore a PostgreSQL database from a custom format archive with pg_restore. Check the destination database name and verify row counts after restoring. A logical backup does not include the server configuration.

title: Postgres connection pool limits
body: A connection pool reuses database sessions. Bound the pool size and connection timeout so a failed database cannot hold every request indefinitely. Each session has its own search path.

title: Postgres transaction isolation
body: Read committed gives each statement a fresh committed snapshot. Repeatable read keeps the transaction snapshot. Serializable transactions may abort and require an explicit application decision about retrying.

title: Postgres vector cosine search
body: The pgvector cosine distance operator compares normalized embeddings. Store the provider, model and dimension with the index. Refuse queries whose embedding identity differs from the stored stamp.

title: SQLite backup snapshot
body: Use the SQLite backup API for a consistent snapshot while other connections remain open. Copying only the main database file can omit transactions still held in the write ahead log.

title: SQLite write ahead log
body: WAL mode lets readers continue while a writer appends transactions. A checkpoint transfers committed pages into the main database. A busy checkpoint does not mean the database is corrupt.

title: SQLite full text ranking
body: FTS5 retrieves token matches and exposes a BM25 rank. Candidate ranking can change with document frequency and query tokenization. Exact title matches need a separate relevance rule.

title: Database schema migrations
body: Apply schema changes in a transaction with an explicit schema version. Reject an unknown future version. A read only connection verifies the version and never attempts to create tables.

title: Database pool outage recovery
body: When the database is unavailable, report a connection error with a bounded deadline. Keep failed requests distinct from empty search results. Recovery must not silently switch to another database.

title: Memory vector identity stamp
body: An embedding index is comparable only with a matching provider model and dimension. Replacing a model requires a fresh index. Preserve the published index until replacement vectors are ready.

title: Memory archive history
body: Archiving memory hides an item from ordinary recall while retaining its body and history. Restoration should preserve authorship. An archive operation is different from permanently deleting a record.

title: Memory hybrid recall fusion
body: Hybrid recall retrieves lexical and vector candidates, then combines their ranks. Deduplicate by item identity before returning results. Preserve a keyword fallback when query embedding is unavailable.

title: Terminal literal paste delivery
body: Wrap literal pasted text in bracketed paste boundaries. Keep the composer payload intact across quotes and newlines. A terminal echo proves bytes appeared on screen but does not prove the agent accepted a user turn.

title: Terminal submit confirmation
body: A written payload needs confirmation from the exact agent session. If confirmation is unavailable, retain the uncertain state. Never resend the payload merely because the submit acknowledgement was delayed.

title: Terminal resize events
body: Send the new row and column dimensions to the pseudo terminal when its visible viewport changes. Keep the screen model and process dimensions aligned. Hidden panes should not overwrite a visible pane's dimensions.

title: Terminal output backpressure
body: Bound output buffers during a large stream and consume chunks incrementally. Avoid serializing the entire scrollback on every update. Apply backpressure before memory growth blocks interactive input.

title: Agent session ownership
body: Every agent tab owns one claimed provider session. Resolve model and status from that session's records. The newest global session can belong to another tab even when both share a working directory.

title: Agent restart continuity
body: Restart the agent with the same verified session when continuity is requested. Preserve uncertain input without replaying it. A new process identifier does not imply a new conversation.

title: Provider capability routing
body: Choose an agent transport from its declared capabilities. A provider may expose a pseudo terminal or a chat runtime. Core routing should ask what the provider supports instead of matching its display name.

title: Agent hook environment
body: Provider hooks receive the API address token and tab identity from the launch environment. Keep hook content identical across application instances. A baked in endpoint can route a development event into production.

title: Terminal keyboard shortcuts
body: Use physical keyboard codes for application shortcuts and map Control to Command on macOS where appropriate. Respect composition events so an input method can finish text before a shortcut acts.

title: Terminal scrollback search
body: Search the terminal scrollback without changing the process input. Keep result positions stable while new chunks arrive. A screen search result is not an authoritative conversation history record.

title: Agent command readiness
body: Use lifecycle events and the provider protocol to establish readiness. Elapsed time does not prove a prompt can accept input. Initial bootstrap delivery belongs to the lifecycle owned pseudo terminal.

title: Terminal process cleanup
body: Identify the exact process and instance before cleanup. Development and production have different listeners. An ambiguous process identity is a reason to preserve the process and report the uncertainty.

title: Mesh peer authentication
body: Authenticate a paired peer before accepting remote commands. Revocation blocks future admission. A peer advertisement alone does not grant permission to execute a task or read private data.

title: Mesh connection revocation
body: Disconnecting a mesh peer records a revocation and removes the active edge. Reconnection requires fresh approval. An offline peer receives the signed removal after it reconnects.

title: Webhook request signatures
body: Verify the signature against the exact request body before decoding a webhook command. Reject an invalid signature. Keep the secret separate from command arguments and application logs.

title: HTTP readiness endpoint
body: A listener can accept connections before the service is ready. The health response carries startup phase and build identity. Compare the running build with the intended source revision before diagnosing behavior.

title: HTTP request timeout budget
body: Bound connection and response waits with a request deadline. A timeout is a failure bound and never a readiness signal. Preserve whether a command failed before delivery or has an uncertain result.

title: Loopback listener binding
body: Bind local development listeners to loopback explicitly. A wildcard listener exposes additional interfaces. A private service should publish only addresses whose listener and authentication have been verified.

title: Telegram reply routing
body: Reply through the bridge that delivered the message so the sender receives it in the original thread. A local tab response alone does not deliver an answer to the remote conversation.

title: Remote task result delivery
body: A remote worker reports the accepted task identity and its own commit revision. Transfer the lane through an authenticated bundle. Preserve ancestry through a real merge instead of replaying individual patches.

title: Encrypted neighbor messages
body: Encrypt message envelopes before sending them to a relay. The receiving installation verifies the sender and decrypts locally. The relay stores ciphertext and must not receive private conversation bodies.

title: Network secret storage
body: Keep service credentials in the local secret store and read them through the authorized interface. Do not include secret values in persistent memory, terminal command arguments or cross machine telemetry.

title: Streaming response cancellation
body: Cancel the exact request when its owner closes the stream. Preserve completed result events already received. A disconnected client must not leave an unbounded background response accumulating in memory.

title: DNS cache invalidation
body: An expired DNS answer requires resolution before establishing a new connection. Existing sessions can remain usable. Keep cached address lifetime distinct from service authentication and application readiness.
